open_points.subject: State 0 acceptance
open_points.text: “Reopened by the owner” and “State 0 closes again when its question rounds are clear; the owner then accepts it as a whole” conflict with “None open” and the statement that round 18 was accepted.
open_points.question: Is this revision of State 0 still reopened, or has the owner accepted and closed it as a whole?
options: Remain reopened pending explicit whole-document acceptance
Treat the accepted answers and absence of open questions as closing State 0
open_points.default_guess: Remain reopened until the owner explicitly accepts the whole revision.

open_points.subject: Authority of R0-61 to R0-67
open_points.text: The status says the vNext requirements and answers “are recorded as R0-24 to R0-60”, while the document relies on accepted decisions R0-61 to R0-67.
open_points.question: Are R0-61 to R0-67 part of the authoritative vNext decision set governed by the status section?
options: Include R0-61 to R0-67 in the authoritative reopening
Treat them as proposals pending inclusion in the accepted whole
open_points.default_guess: Include R0-61 to R0-67 as authoritative because their headings and the Open questions section say they were accepted.

open_points.subject: Service writes to Registry-owned identity
open_points.text: “Every other service names a project by the Registry's identity and reads that identity as a snapshot; none of them writes it back” conflicts with Cabinet Kernel being allowed to add rooms and services being allowed to publish and withdraw artifact pointers, all of which are listed as Registry-owned identity.
open_points.question: Are service operations allowed to create rooms and change artifact-pointer state in Registry, or is Registry identity writable only by the owner?
options: Allow only the explicitly declared room and artifact commands from services
Make every non-owner service read-only for Registry identity
Remove rooms and artifact pointers from what ‘none of them writes it back’ covers
open_points.default_guess: Allow the explicitly declared commands and interpret “writes it back” as forbidding consumers from replacing or correcting identity snapshots.

open_points.subject: Owner sign-in boundary
open_points.text: “Every request on either is authenticated; anything not authenticated is refused” and “No operation of Registry answers an unauthenticated caller” coexist with “The owner signs in to the owner interface with the owner credential and gets a protected session.”
open_points.question: What unauthenticated action accepts the owner credential, and what does it return or refuse?
options: Define sign-in as the sole pre-session authentication exception
Use authentication performed by an external system before any Registry request
Require the credential on every owner-interface request without a sign-in operation
open_points.default_guess: Define a sign-in request as the sole exception; valid credentials create a protected session and invalid credentials are refused.

open_points.subject: Physical location of the agent
open_points.text: R0-28 calls the home server “a machine on which no agent runs”, while R0-48 says “The agent runs in a separate VM Agent on the same server.”
open_points.question: Does the no-agent trust boundary apply to the physical home server or only to VM Platform?
options: No agent runs on the physical home server
The agent may run on the server but never inside or with administrative access to VM Platform
open_points.default_guess: Apply the boundary to VM Platform; the agent runs in the isolated VM Agent on the same physical server.

open_points.subject: Agent call with no project id and no active project
open_points.text: R0-46 says the active project is “the default when the agent names none”, but no action states what happens when the agent names no project and the session has no active project.
open_points.question: What observable result occurs when an agent-authority operation omits `project_id` and the session has no active project?
options: Refuse because no project was selected
Use the sole granted project if exactly one exists
Require every operation to name a project unless an active project exists
open_points.default_guess: Refuse with the same non-disclosing access failure used for an unavailable project.

open_points.subject: Clear an active project
open_points.text: R0-46 says “the owner may also clear it”, but the action “change the active project or revoke a project” does not state an input, output or failure for clearing the active project without revoking it.
open_points.question: Which action clears a session's active project, and what does it return or refuse?
options: Treat clearing as a mode of change-active with a null project
Add a distinct clear-active action
Allow clearing only as the consequence of revocation or project erasure
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as a change-active operation selecting no project and return the updated session access.

open_points.subject: Session access mutation concurrency
open_points.text: The session access exposes an “access version”, while grant, answer-request, change-active and revoke actions do not say whether that version must be supplied or what a stale change does.
open_points.question: Which session-access mutations are conditional on the access version, and what happens on a stale version?
options: Require the access version for every owner mutation of a session
Expose the version for observation only and serialize mutations without a stale check
Require it only for answering requests and changing or revoking access
open_points.default_guess: Require the current access version for every owner mutation and refuse stale changes without modifying access.

open_points.subject: Granting an already granted project
open_points.text: “the project joins the session's granted set” gives no output or failure when it is already in that set, including when the owner asks to make it active.
open_points.question: What happens when the owner grants a project the session already has?
options: Return the access unchanged, applying an active-project choice if requested
Refuse it as already granted
Create a new access version even if no effective state changes
open_points.default_guess: Return the existing grant unchanged and apply the requested active-project change if needed.

open_points.subject: Answering a request with an ineligible project
open_points.text: “granting adds the project the owner picks from the catalogue” lists only “a request no longer pending” as failure, while the separate grant action refuses an unknown or archived project.
open_points.question: Does answering a request by granting an unknown, archived or already granted project fail, clear the request, or apply the ordinary grant rules?
options: Apply all grant eligibility rules and leave the request pending on failure
Apply the rules but clear the request even when granting fails
Allow any project visible in the catalogue, including archived projects
open_points.default_guess: Apply the ordinary grant rules atomically and leave the request pending if the selected grant is refused.

open_points.subject: Repeated restriction transitions
open_points.text: “restrict or lift a restriction on a customer” states no result for restricting an already restricted customer or lifting a customer who is not restricted.
open_points.question: Are repeated restrict and lift requests idempotent, or are they refused?
options: Return the unchanged Customer
Refuse an invalid current-state transition
Record a new revision and audit entry despite no effective change
open_points.default_guess: Return the Customer unchanged without creating a new revision or audit change.

open_points.subject: Relationship end date
open_points.text: “The Customer marked as ended on that date” does not say whether the date is supplied by the owner or recorded by Registry from the action time.
open_points.question: Where does the relationship end date come from, and may it be changed by ending the relationship again?
options: Owner supplies an effective date
Registry records the acceptance date
Registry records both an effective date and the action time
open_points.default_guess: The owner supplies the effective end date, while Registry timestamps the change separately.

open_points.subject: Repeated end and resume transitions
open_points.text: “end or resume a customer relationship” gives no observable result for ending an already ended relationship or resuming one that is not ended.
open_points.question: Are repeated end or resume requests idempotent, refused, or allowed to change the recorded end date?
options: Return the unchanged Customer
Refuse the invalid current-state transition
Permit another end request to replace the end date
open_points.default_guess: Return unchanged for an identical transition, but require an explicit correction rule to replace an existing end date.

open_points.subject: Erasing an already anonymised project
open_points.text: An anonymised project remains with id and status `archived`, so it still satisfies the stated precondition for “erase an archived project”; no result is given for another anonymise or a later whole deletion.
open_points.question: May an anonymised project later be deleted whole, and what happens if anonymisation is requested again?
options: Allow later whole deletion and make repeated anonymisation idempotent
Refuse every later erase action once anonymised
Allow repeated owner choice between anonymised and deleted states
open_points.default_guess: Allow a later whole deletion and return unchanged for repeated anonymisation.

open_points.subject: Revision checks on owner-interface changes
open_points.text: R0-29 says “Every change” made against an older revision is refused, while R0-35 assigns revisions only to projects and customers after the object revision is removed, and many owner changes have no revision or stale failure.
open_points.question: Which owner-interface changes are revision-conditional: only project and customer record changes, or also archive, restriction, relationship, session access, artifact and audit changes?
options: Only mutations of records that explicitly carry a revision
Every owner change, using record revisions or an equivalent version
Project/customer changes plus session changes using its access version
open_points.default_guess: Use project and customer revisions for their mutations and the access version for session mutations; other actions need their own explicit concurrency rule only if required.

open_points.subject: Agent-visible artifact references
open_points.text: The agent projection contains “artifact pointers” and the agent may read the latest pointer, while a pointer contains caller-supplied `uri` or `payload_ref`; the same projection promises “no personal value”, but no rule prevents personal data from appearing in those references.
open_points.question: How does Registry guarantee that artifact-pointer data returned to an agent contains no `personal_data` value?
options: Return only non-reference pointer metadata to the agent
Require and enforce that `uri` and `payload_ref` never contain personal data
Classify each pointer field and redact fields above agent authority
Do not allow agents to read artifact pointers
open_points.default_guess: Return only pointer metadata whose declared class is allowed, omitting `uri` and `payload_ref` unless their contract guarantees they contain no personal data.

open_points.subject: Audit event coverage
open_points.text: R0-58 records “only significant changes of state” and names broad categories such as “changes to projects and customer records”, without saying which primary actions count, particularly room changes, artifact publication or withdrawal, session registration, active-project changes and access requests.
open_points.question: Exactly which primary actions create audit entries?
options: Every accepted state-changing primary action
Only the categories literally enumerated in R0-58
A separately enumerated subset of actions judged significant
open_points.default_guess: Enumerate the subset explicitly; include project/customer mutations, room changes, grants/revocations, restrictions, relationship changes and erasures, but exclude artifact history and transient access requests unless the owner says otherwise.

open_points.subject: Audit target for session grants and revocations
open_points.text: The audit fields name “the project or customer”, while R0-58 requires entries for “granting and revoking an agent session's projects”; no stored fact identifies the affected session.
open_points.question: Must an audit entry for a grant or revocation identify the agent session as well as the project?
options: Store both session id and project id
Store only the project id
Describe the session only inside the change label
open_points.default_guess: Store both the session identity and project identity as structured audit targets.

open_points.subject: Audit outcomes for refused changes
open_points.text: R0-37 says an audit entry carries “the outcome”, while R0-58 says the log records “changes of state” and excludes ordinary calls; a refused request makes no state change.
open_points.question: Are refused attempts at significant actions written to the audit log, and if not, what non-success outcomes can an entry contain?
options: Audit both accepted and refused significant actions
Audit only accepted state changes
Audit selected refusals as infrastructure security events outside Registry
open_points.default_guess: Audit accepted significant state changes only; refused attempts are not audit entries unless a separate explicit security-event requirement is added.
